summary: This article explains how roots take in water, how it rises through the stem to the leaves, and why plants need water to make food and stay firm.
introduce: Write the key term “absorb” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “How Plants Drink Water” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: to take in or soak up something, like a liquid
the thin tubes inside a plant that carry water up from the roots
water that has turned into a gas you usually cannot see

challengeTerms.def: tiny openings in a leaf that let gases and water vapor in and out
the loss of water as vapor from the leaves of a plant
the way particles of the same thing stick together

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a plant's roots are its most important part? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine you are a drop of water. Describe your trip through a plant from the soil to the air.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review absorb, xylem, and vapor, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses stomata, transpiration, and cohesion to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
